**Music now plays from a SoundFont on every system.** The scores play through
sampled General MIDI instruments, close to the Roland Sound Canvas the DOOM
music was written on. The bundled bank is GeneralUser GS, so the downloads are
about 32 MB bigger. Put your own `.sf2` bank in the `soundfonts` folder beside
`doom.cfg` and it is used instead, or launch with `-soundfont bank.sf2`.

**F4 → Sound → Music** picks the music device: SoundFont (the new default),
OPL, or on the Mac the system synthesizer. `-opl`, `-soundfont` and
`-systemsynth` pick one for a single session.

**OPL music rebuilt from scratch.** The FM synthesis of DOS sound cards was
rewritten from Yamaha's chip manual and the published descriptions of DOOM's
instrument and music formats. Every note is now within 2.5 cents of true pitch.
`doom-music-render` writes any WAD's songs to WAV files for listening, without
starting the game.

**The F4 panel uses DOOM's own font**, taken from the WAD you play, in place
of the old text-mode font.

**Removed: the "Pixel-art upscale (xBR)" sprite option.** Sprites are crisp
(the default) or soft. If you had xBR selected, you get crisp sprites.

**New license: GPL version 3.** Duct-Tape DOOM is now under the GNU GPL 3, with
one added term: copies and derivative works must keep the attribution
"Duct-Tape DOOM — https://github.com/robongrui/duct-tape-doom" (`NOTICE.txt`).
id Software's DOOM code was released in 1999 under "GPL 2 or any later
version", which allows this. Each download's `licenses` folder now lists every
outside part and its license (`THIRD_PARTY.md`), including the extra notices
inside SDL.

**Complete source download.** Each release now has
`DuctTapeDOOM-source.tar.gz`: the game's code plus the exact SDL, Nuked OPL3
and TinySoundFont sources and the SoundFont it was built with, so it builds
without an internet connection.
